title: Refrigerant Leak & Glass Fracture Thermal Simulation
description: A commercial refrigerator sits in a cold storage room with a broken glass window. The user must manage the refrigerator's material properties (insulation layers, door seal integrity, coolant flow rate) and the broken window's glass fragment materials (thermal conductivity, transparency, structural bonding) to maintain a target internal temperature. Energy conservation governs heat exchange: heat leaking through the broken window raises ambient temperature, stressing the refrigerator. Users can undo/redo any material adjustment and must balance multiple coupled inputs to reach equilibrium.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) implementing an interactive thermal-materials simulation. Load CommercialRefrigerator.glb centered at (0,0,0) and GlassBrokenWindow.glb positioned as a wall panel at (-3,1.5,2) facing the refrigerator. Use OrbitControls with the camera at (5,3,6) looking at origin. Add ambient light (0.4) and a directional light simulating outdoor sun through the broken window. Implement a right-side HTML/CSS control panel with these interactive material parameters: (1) Refrigerator insulation R-value slider (1-10), (2) Door seal integrity slider (0-100%), (3) Coolant flow rate slider (0-5 L/min), (4) Window glass fragment thermal conductivity slider (0.5-5.0 W/mK), (5) Window repair bonding percentage slider (0-100%), (6) Ambient outdoor temperature input (-10 to 45°C). Implement energy conservation: Q_leak through window = k_glass * (1 - bond%) * (T_outdoor - T_room) and Q_fridge_loss = (1/R) * (1 - seal%) * (T_room - T_internal). Coolant removes heat: Q_cool = flow_rate * 2000. Each simulation tick updates T_room and T_internal via these coupled equations. Display live temperature readouts for T_room and T_internal. Visually tint the refrigerator mesh blue-to-red based on T_internal (target: -2°C to 4°C shown as green). Tint the broken window fragments from blue (cold outside) to orange (hot outside) based on heat flux. Add emissive glow to window cracks proportional to leak rate. Implement full undo/redo (Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y) storing snapshots of all six parameter values and restoring them with visual updates. Add Undo and Redo buttons in the panel. The user goal displayed at top: adjust all six parameters across 10+ steps to stabilize T_internal between -2°C and 4°C while T_room stays below 15°C. Show a success banner when both conditions hold for 5 consecutive ticks. Ensure all meshes cast and receive shadows with a ground plane.
